message.reasoning_content:
Implement merge. Signature: merge(self, ranges). Merge closed integer intervals; overlapping or adjacent? Test: [[5,7],[1,3],[2,4]] -> [(1,4),(5,7)]. [1,3] and [2,4] overlap merge to (1,4). [5,7] separate (4<5, gap). Whether adjacent merges (3,4 touching) is not tested. Standard "merge intervals" typically merges if start <= current_end. With closed intervals, [1,3] and [4,6] — do they merge? Ambiguous. I'll merge when start <= end (overlap or touching) — hmm, for closed integer intervals [1,3] and [4,6] the integers are distinct sets, so touching shouldn't merge. But typical leetcode merge-intervals merges if start <= end, which for [1,3],[4,6] does not merge (4 > 3). So overlap only. That's the safest: merge if start <= cur_end. Let's implement.

Empty returns []. Sorted by start, list of tuples.

Maybe accept iterables generally.
